source.title: World Modeling in Transformers
source.authors: P. Beckmann; Matthieu Queloz; André Freitas

record.file_problem: None noted; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures superposition among intersection representations and its effect on navigation, but it does not measure individual neurons responding to unrelated inputs or test any listed neuron-polysemanticity version.
record.gate_note: The paper's own results concern intersection feature directions in TaxiGPT's residual stream, not neuron-level responses or meanings. Those feature-geometry and intervention results are recorded as related findings under fits_no_version. Results cited from other work are not included as rows.
record.test_reason: The paper studies superposition among diff-means intersection feature directions in TaxiGPT's residual stream, and how their interference causes illegal moves. It never examines individual neurons or reports whether neurons respond to unrelated inputs. It also does not compare activations, architectures or measurement choices for neuron polysemanticity. No version of the claim is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors find that TaxiGPT holds a faithful, causally used internal map, plus a goal compass. Its failures come from localization errors caused by interference between superposed intersection features out of distribution. Affordance packing limits the damage. They also propose mechanistic indicators showing world-modeling capacities emerge at different training stages, and argue for studying world modeling rather than asking whether a model has a world model.
record.recipe_differences: The paper analyzes intersection feature directions and causal navigation interventions in TaxiGPT; it does not apply the neuron-response methods or SoLU comparison from the original sources.
record.method_sensitivity: not stated for neuron-polysemanticity measurements; the reported feature analyses use specified layers, including layer 18 for intersection superposition.

fits_no_version.finding: Thousands of intersection feature directions overlap in a low-dimensional residual-stream subspace and are grouped by shared legal moves. Interference among them under weak position writes and noise causes illegal moves; removing noise or strengthening the write repairs this.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In TaxiGPT, superposed intersection representations interfere with localization and cause behavioral errors, while packing by shared affordances mitigates many of them.

fits_no_version.finding: During training the position code expands (d90 rises from 1 to 204, nearest-neighbor angle rises) while affordance packing peaks early and then relaxes. Better-performing models show less superposed features (Table 1, Table 16). No row records this.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Feature-direction superposition decreases as training progresses and model quality improves (residual-stream features, not neurons).

record.problems: The evidence is from a TaxiGPT model trained on a finite Manhattan navigation task, and the paper studies intersection directions rather than individual neurons. Results on neuron-level polysemanticity cannot be inferred from these measurements.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant results omitted; cited findings from other studies are not recorded as rows.

untested.parts: No vision models; no neuron-level responses.
No MLP neuron analysis or per-layer share of polysemantic neurons; only residual-stream feature directions.
Superposition is shown for feature directions (4,516 directions in about 244 dimensions), but it is never linked to neuron polysemanticity.
Cross-model and training comparisons concern feature-direction dimensionality, not the share of polysemantic neurons; no activation-function comparison.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's T6 and versions=none for all rows are confirmed. The 'discusses' relation fits loosely: the paper discusses feature superposition (Elhage et al.) but never mentions polysemantic neurons. Row r9's 'partial' state is relative to the paper's other edits, not to any claim version. Rows r5–r11 are repair interventions on the study's own failure categories, not measures of the phenomenon.

versions.untested_parts: Neuron responses to multiple unrelated image inputs; vision models.
Polysemantic MLP neurons in language models and their prevalence across layers.
Whether polysemantic neurons arise because features outnumber neurons and are packed together.
Polysemantic neurons without capacity pressure, including causes such as initialization, regularization, or training noise.
Changes in the share of polysemantic neurons across activations, architectures, or regularization, including SoLU and modern convnets.
Whether putatively polysemantic neurons actually detect a shared feature or related jobs.
Whether neuron-polysemanticity judgments depend on activation range or explanation scoring.
